rules.title: Traffic ordinances
rules.current_text: A. State law: The County is responsible. B. Union County policy: The County adopts consenting resolutions after enactment of local ordinances. C. Comment: The Commissioners have concurred with all municipal traffic ordinances on County roads with the exception of parking meter installation and regulation.
rules.current_text_summary: The county is responsible under state law; county policy is to adopt consenting resolutions after local traffic ordinances are enacted; the Commissioners state that they have concurred with municipal traffic ordinances on county roads except parking-meter regulation.

rules.citation: Union County Code 138-8 and 138-36, Schedule VI
rules.title: Vehicle weight limits

current_text.section_138_8: Trucks over four tons' gross weight are hereby excluded from the streets or parts of streets described in Schedule VI (§ 138-36), except for the pickup and delivery of materials on such streets, said Schedule VI (§ 138-36) being attached to and made a part of this chapter.
current_text.section_138_36_relevant_text: In accordance with the provisions of § 138-8, trucks over four tons' gross weight are hereby excluded from all streets in the Union County park system except for the pickup and delivery of materials as excepted.

rules.current_text_summary: Trucks over four tons gross weight are excluded from the streets in Schedule VI except for pickup and delivery on those streets. Schedule VI applies to streets in the Union County park system.
rules.terminal_access_exception: No general terminal exception; only pickup/delivery on a scheduled park street.
rules.current_status: present in county code updated through January 2026

rules.citation: Union County Code 138-9 and 138-37, Schedule VII
rules.title: Truck routes

current_text.section_138_9: Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40:67-16.1, the streets or parts of streets described in Schedule VII (§ 138-37), attached to and made a part of this chapter, are hereby designated as routes for trucks over four tons. All trucks having a total combined gross weight of vehicle plus load in excess of four tons shall be excluded from all streets except from those streets which form a part of the system of truck routes.
current_text.section_138_37: In accordance with the provisions of § 138-9 the following streets or parts of streets are hereby designated as routes for trucks over four tons: Name of Street; Location; (Reserved).

rules.current_text_summary: Section 138-9 excludes trucks whose combined vehicle and load exceed four tons from streets other than designated truck routes, but the required Schedule VII contains no roads and is marked Reserved.

vehicle_scope.threshold: combined vehicle plus load over 4 tons

rules.current_status: text remains in county code updated through January 2026
rules.later_amendment_effect: no amendment resolving the empty schedule was found
rules.open_issue: Obtain underlying Ordinance No. 160 and a written county interpretation before treating this as either a countywide ban or a corridor designation.

rules.title: Truck access and reasonable access to terminals
rules.current_text_summary: The chapter governs double-trailer combinations and standard trucks wider than 96 inches but no wider than 102 inches. A 102-inch-wide standard truck may use local unrestricted roads as necessary to reach a terminal by the direct route. Local and county restrictions are preserved.
vehicle_scope: standard trucks greater than 96 inches and not greater than 102 inches wide
rules.terminal_access_exception: Direct terminal access is allowed only as stated for the covered class; it does not supersede municipal ordinances, county resolutions, weight limits, or other restrictions.
rules.current_status: readopted November 30, 2022; amendments effective January 3, 2023; expires November 30, 2029
rules.later_amendment_effect: The 2023 text narrows the local-unrestricted-road sentence to a 102-inch-wide standard truck rather than both covered classes.

rules.authority: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
rules.citation: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10, Subrules 34-035, 34-045, 34-046, 34-090, and 34-105
rules.title: Terminal highway weight, dimensions, and conditional use
rules.current_text_summary: Marine Terminal Highways are terminal portions PANYNJ makes available for general or limited highway use. Containerized shipments may not exceed 128,000 pounds gross vehicle weight or manufacturer safe working loads. Vehicles over 16 feet 3 inches high or 11 feet wide require terminal-manager approval. Terminal permission is conditional and users must comply with other governmental laws.
rules.terminal_access_exception: No exception to off-terminal law. Terminal permission adds conditions and expressly preserves other governmental requirements.
rules.later_amendment_effect: This May 1, 2026 tariff is later than the March 10, 2026 edition located during the audit.

rules.authority: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
rules.citation: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10, Subrules 34-1000, 34-1100, and 34-1121
rules.title: Drayage Truck Registry and gate check
rules.current_text_summary: An on-road vehicle over 33,000 pounds GVWR serving a PANYNJ terminal for cargo movement is a Drayage Truck, subject to listed exclusions. Covered drayage trucks must be registered before entry, and terminal facilities must check registry compliance.
rules.terminal_access_exception: none; terminal business is necessary but does not itself satisfy registry or gate requirements

rules.authority: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
rules.title: Operating hours for overweight or overwidth containerized cargo
rules.current_text_summary: The current operating window is 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
rules.terminal_access_exception: not an exception; this is an additional operating window
rules.current_status: current PANYNJ truck-information page checked July 26, 2026
rules.later_amendment_effect: operational hours can change independently of the tariff
